audit_result.proof_trace: No rate limiting middleware, package, or logic exists anywhere in the codebase (grep for rate.*limit/throttle returns zero matches; package.json has no rate limiting dependency). The Express app registers only cors and authMiddleware globally — no request-frequency control on any path. The unauthenticated /health endpoint (L38-65) directly invokes client.guilds.fetch(guildId) per request, providing an external-attacker-accessible vector to exhaust Discord's bot API rate limit quota.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An attacker floods GET /health with concurrent requests from any IP; each request triggers a live Discord REST call (guilds.fetch), saturating the bot's Discord rate limit bucket and causing all subsequent Discord operations (role assignments via /api/roles/sync, /api/roles/sync-all, etc.) to receive 429 responses from Discord, effectively disabling the bot's core functionality.

PROP-api-request-inv-009.text: API endpoints must enforce rate limiting to prevent abuse and Discord API rate limit exhaustion.
PROP-api-request-inv-009.assertion: forall req from ip: count(req, ip, window) <= RATE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
